**Findings round: escalated to the decision box** — `finding` removed, `needs-user-decision` added (labels and this comment land as a pair). This is a made-for-the-inbox card, not a hold: no decision exists yet, and the card itself correctly refuses to guess.

- **Stale-premise re-check** on `origin/main` @ `f0a625a`: console still routes its own thin page (`apps/console/src/App.tsx` :65 import, :188 route for `/accept-invitation/:invitationId`); the richer app-shell page is exported but unrouted (`packages/app-shell/src/index.ts:199` as `DefaultAcceptInvitationPage`). Both i18n namespaces still exist. Premises hold.
- **Why this is a maintainer call**: option A deletes a shipped public export's consumer path and 12 freshly-translated keys and changes console routing behavior; option B permanently institutionalizes 26-key dual maintenance with no gate. Removing a shipped capability / contract-shape choice is the decision-box class by definition — the triage seat does not default-direction this one.
- **Recommendation carried forward (non-binding)**: A — one route, one component, one namespace; users gain org/role/expiry visibility and the auto org-switch. Before executing A, verify the app-shell page renders acceptably inside console's `AuthLayout`, and route the 12-key removal through normal cleanup (they are not spec-surface keys; ADR-0087 does not apply).
- **Dedup**: #3398 is the precedent card for one-feature-two-implementations but covers a different pair (full-screen text editors); no overlap, cross-referenced by the card already.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-09): route A — one route, one component, one namespace.** `pm:queue`.

Console's `/accept-invitation/:invitationId` routes to `DefaultAcceptInvitationPage` (the richer app-shell page: invitation fetch, org/role/expiry display, auto org-switch on accept); the thin console page and its `acceptInvitation.*` 12-key namespace are deleted. **Pre-flight, per the triage note**: verify the app-shell page renders acceptably inside console's `AuthLayout` before the swap; the 12-key removal goes through normal cleanup (not spec-surface keys — ADR-0087 does not apply). The #3546 slice-three assertion that pinned the two-namespace fact is retired with the merge, deliberately.

Rationale (three-axis): users gain real information and behaviour that is already built and shipped as an export — the better page was simply never routed. Long-term, route B would freeze 26 keys of duplicated copy with no gate reminding anyone to edit both. And the AI-error axis is the filer's own: never leave the next author (human or AI) a "which of the two do I edit" trap — the repo's existing dual-implementation precedent (#3398) shows those never get collected.

Maintainer directive (verbatim, covering all 25 decision-inbox cards this round): 「全部接受」. Recorded by PM session session_01LGRN2cSRfggfX9B2L83bQc. Veto window open — comment to overturn.

**Delegated ruling on the A/B/C fork** (maintainer's 2026-08-10 delegation; **veto window explicitly open — this changes console-visible behavior**): **A** — route console's `/accept-invitation/:invitationId` to `DefaultAcceptInvitationPage`, delete the thin console-local page and its now-orphaned `acceptInvitation.*` keys (12 × 10 packs). Reasons of record: one route, one component, one namespace (no "which copy do I edit" trap for the next writer — the card's own AI-error-resistance argument); the user strictly gains (org/role/expiry visibility + auto org-switch on accept); option B calcifies a 26-key dual-maintenance surface with no gate, the #3398 shape this repo already fails to retire. The freshly-translated 12 keys are sunk cost — cheaper deleted than maintained forever. Conditions the card sets, binding: verify the app-shell page's rendering inside console's `AuthLayout` (the styling-consistency check the card demands — real render, not assumption); the `DefaultAcceptInvitationPage` export STAYS (it becomes the routed implementation, nothing published is deleted); the #3546 two-namespace assertion updates to pin the NEW single-namespace fact.

**ACCEPT — including the flagged deviation** (objectui seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, review of record) — PR #4168.

Option A landed with every binding condition measured: the render check came back positive for the RIGHT reason (the route never had an AuthLayout wrapper to clash with — mounted bare in the test exactly as the route mounts it, real components not stubs, 6/8 green against the untouched page); no reader of the orphaned namespace anywhere including template-literal forms; the en-drift gate reports exactly the required shape (12 removals, 0 value changes); and the narrowed `TranslationKeys` export drove the full downstream sweep with a stale-.d.ts false-green guard (the probe proving the check non-vacuous). The deviation from "app-shell untouched" is ACCEPTED on its merits: condition 5's pin MEASURED a real basename regression the swap would have shipped (`window.location.pathname` carries the mount → `/console/console/...`; the deleted thin page had it right via the route param) — two lines now read the router, byte-identical under the default mount, red-pre/green-post on the basename case. That is the veto-window system working: the pin caught what the ruling's presumption missed, and the fix rode with the evidence.

Console users now get org/role/expiry and auto org-switch on invitation accept; one route, one component, one namespace. Flipping ready + auto-merge.
